<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par123 />Thus {{GHGheb|text=בָּקָר|translate=cattle, oxen}}<ref>The plural form {{GHGheb|text=בְּקָרִים}} from {{GHGheb|text=בָּקָר}} is found only in very late Hebrew, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=10|verse=37}} (where according to the Mantua edition, Ginsburg, &c., even {{GHGheb|text=צֹאנֵ֫ינוּ|translate=our sheep}}, is also to be read; Baer, however, has {{GHGheb|text=צֹאנֵ֫נוּ}}), and {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=4|verse=3}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=6|verse=12}} read, with Hitzig, {{GHGheb|text=בַּבָּקָר יָם}}.</ref> (even joined with numerals, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=37}} {{GHGheb|text=חֲמִשָּׁה בָקָר|translate=five head of cattle}}), but {{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹר|translate=an ox}}; {{GHGheb|text=צֹאן|translate=small cattle}}, i.e. sheep and goats (μῆλα), cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=שִׁבְעַת אַלְפֵי־צֹאן|translate=seven thousand sheep}}; but {{GHGheb|text=שֶׂה|translate=a single head of small cattle}} (a sheep or a goat). Other more or less common collectives are: {{GHGheb|text=זִיז}} (prop. that which prowls or roams) ''wild beasts'', {{GHGheb|text=טַף}} (perhaps prop. ''tripping'') ''a number of little children''; {{GHGheb|text=דֶּ֫שֶׁא|translate=fresh green herb}}, i.e. young plants, {{GHGheb|text=יֶ֫רֶק|translate=green}}, i.e. vegetation in general; {{GHGheb|text=עוֹף|translate=birds, fowl}}; {{GHGheb|text=רֶ֫כֶב|translate=chariots}} or ''cavalcade'', {{GHGheb|text=רִמָּה|translate=worms}}, {{GHGheb|text=רֶ֫מֶשׂ|translate=creeping things}} (of small creatures), {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫רֶץ|translate=swarming things}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|123|b}}
(''b'') The collective use of substantives which at the same time serve as {{GHGterm|nomina unitatis}}; thus, {{GHGheb|text=אָדָם}} (never in plur.) means both ''man'' (homo) and ''men'' (homines); {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ|translate=a man}} (vir) and ''men'' (viri); {{GHGheb|text=אִשָּׁה|translate=woman}} and ''women'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=21|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=6}}); {{GHGheb|text=אַרְבֶּה|translate=a locust}}, but usually ''a swarm of locusts''; {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫פֶשׁ|translate=soul}} and ''souls'' (persons); {{GHGheb|text=מַקֵּל|translate=staff}} and ''staves'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=37}}); {{GHGheb|text=עַ֫יִט|translate=a bird of prey}} and ''birds of prey''; {{GHGheb|text=עָלֶה|translate=a leaf}} and ''foliage''; {{GHGheb|text=עֵ֫שֶׂב|translate=a plant}} and ''plants, herbs''; {{GHGheb|text=עֵץ|translate=a tree}} and ''trees'' (as it were ''foliage''); {{GHGheb|text=פְּרִי|translate=fruit}} and ''fruits''; {{GHGheb|text=שִׂיחַ|translate=a shrub}} and ''shrubs''; in isolated instances also nouns like {{GHGheb|text=עֶ֫בֶד|translate=man-servant}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁפְחָה|translate=maid-servant}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֲמוֹר|translate=ass}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹר|translate=ox}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=6}}).—On the singular (especially of gentilic names) with the article (which may, however, be omitted in poetry, cf. e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=12|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=חָסִיד}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=11|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=יוֹעֵץ}}) to include all individuals of the same species, cf. {{GHGpar|126|l}}. On the special meaning of the plurals formed from certain collectives, see {{GHGpar|124|l}}.

(''c'') The feminine ending; see {{GHGpar|122|s}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|123|c}}
(''d'') The repetition of single words, and even of whole groups of words, especially to express entirety, or in a distributive sense. The following cases are more particularly to be noticed:

1. The repetition of one or more words to express the idea of ''every, all'', as {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם יוֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=10}}, &c., ''day'' by ''day, every day''; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנָה שָׁנָה|translate=year}} by ''year'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=14|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ אִישׁ|translate=every}} man, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=36|verse=4}}; with {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} before each, as {{GHGheb|text=בַּבֹּ֫קֶר בַּבֹּ֫קֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=21}} ''every morning'' (and similarly before a group of words, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=24|verse=8}}), for which the ''distributive'' {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} is also used, {{GHGheb|text=לַבֹּ֫קֶר לַבֹּ֫קֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=9|verse=27}}, and with ''one'' plural {{GHGheb|text=לַבְּקָרִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=14}}, {{GHGheb|text=לִבְקָרִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=18}} parallel with {{GHGheb|text=לִרְגָעִים|translate=every moment}}. Somewhat different are the instances with {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} before the second word only, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם בְּיוֹם|translate=day}} by ''day'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=12|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה|translate=year by year}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=7}} (but in verse 3 {{GHGheb|text=מִיָּמִים יָמִ֫ימָה}}), {{GHGheb|text=כְּפַ֫עַם בְּפַ֫עַם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=24|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=30|hidebook=1}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=10}} ''as at other times''. Also with the two words united by means of {{GHGterm|wāw copulative}}, {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ וְאִישׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=87|verse=5}}, or {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ וָאִישׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=1|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=דּוֹר וָדוֹר|translate=all generations}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם וָיוֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=3|verse=4}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=8|verse=9}},<section end=par123 /><noinclude>
